texts.li: Two pair beats a pair of twos, which {B_nameDef} learned last night after betting {B_possessive} good coat on the twos. {A_nameDef} has worn the coat every day since, buttoned to the chin, and remarks on how warm it is whenever {B_nameDef} walks past.\n\n{B_nameDef} says the deck was marked, and wants the bet thrown out.

{A_nameDef} won a week of {B_nameDef}'s dinners at dice, fair and square, with three witnesses. Three days in, {B_nameDef} is living on scraps and has started eyeing {A_nameDef}'s plate.\n\n"A bet is a bet," says {A_nameDef}. The others would like the council to step in before someone gets a fork in the hand.

li.label: Make {B_nameDef} pay up
li.outcome: The debt stands. {B_nameDef} paid up in silence, and {A_nameDef} said thank you in a way that didn't help.
li.riskOutcome: The debt stands. {B_nameDef} heard the ruling out, then came across the table swinging.

li.label: Call the bet off
li.outcome: The bet is off. {A_nameDef} gave the winnings back as slowly as it could be done, and hasn't stopped muttering about it.

li.label: Ban gambling in the colony
li.outcome: The council banned gambling and canceled every debt. The cards went into the fire; the dice have not turned up.

li.label: Double or nothing
li.outcome: One more round, with the council watching. {A_nameDef} won that too. {B_nameDef} owes double now, and has gone off on {B_possessive} own.
li.riskOutcome: One more round, with the council watching, and {B_nameDef} won all of it back. People are still talking about the look on {A_nameDef}'s face.

texts.li:
{B_nameDef} went into {A_nameDef}'s room for a borrowed hammer, looked under the bed, and came back out with a list.

{COUNT} {THING}, out of the stores
The two good kitchen knives
Fourteen spoons
The blanket the moths were blamed for
The hammer

{A_nameDef} calls it a collection.

The good chair went missing from the dining room three days ago. {B_nameDef} followed the scuff marks it left across the floor to {A_nameDef}'s door, and found it inside, with a row of spoons laid out on the seat and {COUNT} {THING} under the mattress.\n\n"I was keeping them safe," {A_nameDef} said. {B_nameDef} wants all of it back in the stores by supper.

li.label: Confiscate the lot
li.outcome: Everything went back where it came from, spoons included, and the {THING} to the stockpile. {A_nameDef} sat on {A_possessive} stripped bed for most of the evening.
li.riskOutcome: Half the hoard was out of the room when {A_nameDef} started throwing the other half at the wall.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} keep it
li.outcome: The collection stays where it is. {B_nameDef} has started bringing {B_possessive} own spoon to the table.

li.label: Return half to the stores
li.outcome: Half the hoard went back to the stores, and {A_nameDef} chose which half. The good knives are not in the kitchen.

texts.li: In {A_nameDef}'s dream the fields were burning, then the sky, and people stood in the smoke without faces. {A_nameDef} woke the colony screaming last night, and has described the dream at every meal since.\n\nSome of the others have started watching the horizon.

Three nights running, {A_nameDef} has dreamed of smoke over the walls and a voice counting backward from ten. Each night it gets further. Last night it reached three.\n\nThe night watch has grown jumpy.

li.label: Double the watch
li.outcome: Two on the wall every night now instead of one. {A_nameDef} looks easier for it. The ones pulling the extra shifts look worse.

li.label: Laugh it off at dinner
li.outcome: Someone at dinner asked {A_nameDef} whether the faceless people had at least been polite, and the table laughed. {A_nameDef} hasn't mentioned the dreams since.
li.riskOutcome: The joke went round the table at dinner. {A_nameDef} put down {A_possessive} spoon, walked out past the fields, and kept going.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} hold a ceremony
li.outcome: Each colonist scratched a fear on a scrap of wood and threw it on {A_nameDef}'s fire. A few scratched nothing and threw theirs in anyway. The colony slept through the night.

li.label: Tell {A_nameDef} to keep it quiet
li.outcome: The dreams are no longer told at meals. They still come, and {A_nameDef} still wakes from them, and the people sleeping nearest hear it.

texts.li: Years ago, long before this colony, a band from {FACTION} found {A_nameDef} half-dead in a ditch and fed {A_objective} for a month without asking for a thing. Word has come that they've had a hard season.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to send them silver. It's the colony's silver, so it's the council's call.

{A_nameDef} rarely talks about the years before the colony. Last night, a beer in, {A_nameDef} told how {FACTION} took {A_objective} in when no one else would, and how {A_pronoun} slipped away one morning without a word of thanks.\n\n"I owe them," {A_nameDef} said. "Or we do, if you'll let me pay it out of the colony's silver."

li.label: Send them 100 silver
li.outcome: A hundred silver went to {FACTION}, with a letter {A_nameDef} took two evenings to write. Their thanks came back with the next traveler.
li.riskOutcome: The silver never reached {FACTION}. It went missing somewhere on the road, and so did whoever was carrying it.

li.label: Send 25 silver as a token
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sent 25 silver and a note to {FACTION}, and wrote the note over three times, trying to make it say more than the silver could.

li.label: Send them food instead
li.outcome: Sacks of food went to {FACTION}, who had more use for grain than coin this season. There's a gap on the storeroom shelves where they stood.

li.label: We need it more than they do
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} didn't argue with the council, and has barely said a word to anyone since.

texts.li: Four pieces. {A_nameDef}'s carved wooden bird, the only thing {A_pronoun} still had from home, went off the shelf when {B_nameDef} caught it with a broom handle.\n\n{B_nameDef} keeps saying it was an accident, more often than seems necessary.

{A_nameDef} carried an old pocket watch that hadn't worked in years. {B_nameDef} borrowed it to fix it, as a surprise, and handed it back in a cupped palm.\n\n{A_nameDef} is grieving over a handful of springs. {B_nameDef} is very sorry and would like that to be the end of it.

li.label: {B_nameDef} apologizes publicly
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} stood up at dinner and said sorry to the whole table, staring at a point over {A_nameDef}'s head. {A_nameDef} nodded, and that was enough.
li.riskOutcome: The apology came at dinner, four words long and said to {B_possessive} bowl. {B_nameDef} didn't mean any of them.

li.label: Pay {A_nameDef} 50 silver
li.outcome: Fifty silver from the colony's stores, for the loss. {A_nameDef} put the coins in the same pouch as the broken pieces.

li.label: Have {B_nameDef} make a new one
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spent three evenings on a replacement. {A_nameDef} has put it on the shelf, in the old one's place.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} spent three evenings on a replacement. It came out lopsided and crude, and {B_nameDef} knew it before anyone said so.

li.label: Call it an accident
li.outcome: An accident, the council said. {A_nameDef} has moved everything {A_pronoun} owns to the top shelf, out of {B_nameDef}'s reach.

texts.li: With raiders seen in the hills, {B_nameDef} had the night watch. {A_nameDef} came out in the small hours and found {B_nameDef} curled up against the wall, asleep, {B_possessive} weapon lying in the dirt.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants it dealt with before nightfall.

A large animal snuffled and scratched at the gate for half of last night, and {B_nameDef}, who had the watch, slept through all of it. {A_nameDef} heard it from bed, and came to the council at dawn white with anger.\n\nIt didn't get in. {A_nameDef} wants to know what happens next time.

li.label: Punish {B_nameDef} with extra shifts
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} hauled and scrubbed until dark, and the penance runs on for days yet. Whoever has the watch tonight will be wide awake.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} took the punishment, then took a swing at {A_nameDef} for reporting it.

li.label: Warn {B_nameDef} privately
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} got a private warning and swore it won't happen again. {A_nameDef} has started checking on the watch at night anyway.
li.riskOutcome: The council spoke to {B_nameDef} in private. Two nights later {B_nameDef} was found asleep on watch again, and this time word got around.

li.label: Put {A_nameDef} in charge of the watch
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} stood the first watch together at the gate, until three in the morning. {A_nameDef} runs the roster now, and {B_nameDef}'s name is on it twice a week.

li.label: Let it go this time
li.outcome: The matter was dropped. {A_nameDef} has stopped sleeping well, and keeps getting up to check the gate.
li.riskOutcome: The council let it go, but {A_nameDef} wouldn't. The next argument with {B_nameDef} ended in a fight.

texts.li: {A_nameDef}'s newest sculpture is {B_nameDef}, unmistakably, down to the squint, with a nose half again the size of the real one.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants the thing gone. {A_nameDef} says it's an honest likeness.

{A_nameDef} calls the new piece "{PLACE}". The others recognized {B_nameDef} in it straight away, and laughed.\n\n{B_nameDef} has asked the council, very calmly, to have it removed before {B_nameDef} takes a hammer to it.

li.label: Smash it
li.outcome: The council had the sculpture smashed. {B_nameDef} took a hammer to it, then swept up the pieces, smiling.
li.riskOutcome: The first blow took the nose off. {A_nameDef} turned and walked out before the second, and hasn't come back.

li.label: Keep it on display
li.outcome: The sculpture stays. Visitors ask who it is, and someone always tells them. {B_nameDef} eats with {B_possessive} back to it.
li.riskOutcome: The sculpture stays. {B_nameDef} heard the ruling and went straight for the sculptor.

li.label: Make {A_nameDef} carve an apology piece
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} carved a second {B_nameDef}, this one square-jawed and gazing nobly into the distance. {B_nameDef} grumbled, then moved it to where the light is better.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef}'s apology piece is handsome, square-jawed and noble, and wearing a dunce cap. Things are worse.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has built a homemade fiddle and practices on it every night after the others have gone to bed. {B_nameDef} sleeps on the other side of the wall and hasn't had a full night's sleep in four days.\n\n{B_nameDef} came to the council red-eyed, still holding {B_possessive} pillow.

Every night, just as the colony settles down, the drumming starts. {A_nameDef} says it helps {A_objective} think.\n\n"Four hours last night," {B_nameDef} told the council. "The same six beats, over and over. I counted."

li.label: Ban the night music
li.outcome: The night music is banned. {B_nameDef} slept fourteen hours straight. {A_nameDef} is sulking, and drums on the table at every meal.

li.label: Set quiet hours after midnight
li.outcome: Music until midnight and not a note after. {A_nameDef} stops mid-tune when the hour comes, with a long sigh {B_nameDef} can hear through the wall.
li.riskOutcome: Quiet hours were agreed, but {A_nameDef} keeps playing past midnight, and {B_nameDef} is lying awake again.

li.label: Tell {B_nameDef} to live with it
li.outcome: The music plays on, and {A_nameDef} is slowly getting better at it. {B_nameDef} sleeps with rags stuffed in both ears and is worn out most days.
li.riskOutcome: The music plays on. {B_nameDef} took the ruling back to {B_possessive} room and started breaking things.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have agreed to settle their quarrel with a fight. Fists only, at dawn, behind the stockpile, with anyone who wants to watch.\n\nThey want the council's blessing, mostly so the loser can't complain afterward.

{B_nameDef} threw a glove at {A_nameDef}'s feet this morning. It was a dirty work glove, and {A_nameDef} took that as part of the insult.\n\nThey want to settle it in the yard, with witnesses, if the council will allow it.

li.label: Allow the duel
li.outcome: The duel was held in the yard with a crowd round it. It ended in a split lip, a loose tooth and a handshake both of them meant.

li.label: Forbid it
li.outcome: There will be no duel. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} still glare at each other across every room they share.
li.riskOutcome: The council forbade the duel. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} held it anyway, behind the latrine, with no witnesses and no rules.

li.label: Make them shake hands in public
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} shook hands at the evening meal, in front of the others. Both squeezed hard and neither smiled, but it's done.
li.riskOutcome: The handshake turned into a shoving match, and then into a proper fight, while the onlookers cheered.

li.label: Settle it with a hauling race
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} hauled stone against each other all afternoon and couldn't agree on the final count. They sat together at supper to keep arguing about it.

lines.li: You dropped that one. It doesn't count.

li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} raced each other hauling stone. The loser accused the winner of cheating, and it came to blows.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has opinions about how the colony is run and wants them to count. {A_nameDef} is asking for a formal seat on the council, with a vote, a chair at the head of the table, and a title.\n\n{A_nameDef} has suggested several titles. Most of them begin with "High."

{A_nameDef} pinned a list of demands to the dining room door overnight. Item one is a seat on the council. Items two through eleven assume item one.\n\nPeople are reading it over breakfast, and some of them are nodding.

li.label: Grant {A_nameDef} a title
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} was given the title of Warden, of nothing in particular. {A_nameDef} is delighted with it, and a few of the others are jealous.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} was named Warden and is taking it very seriously. Several people have already been told off for sitting in the wrong chair.

li.label: Refuse the request
li.outcome: Refused. {A_nameDef} heard it without a word, and every door {A_pronoun} has gone through since has been slammed.

li.label: Put {A_nameDef} in charge of the storeroom
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is now in charge of the storeroom and has already relabeled every shelf in it.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} asked for a seat at the table and was given the storeroom keys instead, and took it as an insult.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} sit in on one meeting
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat through four hours of debate about where to dig the new latrine and has withdrawn the request.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} sat through four hours of debate about the latrine and enjoyed all of it. {A_nameDef} now comes to every meeting, invited or not.

texts.li: Two columns are chalked on the workshop wall, one for {A_nameDef}'s hours of work and one for {B_nameDef}'s. {B_nameDef}'s is mostly empty.\n\n{A_nameDef} has started underlining things, and wants the council to come and look.

{A_nameDef} came to the council with dirt up to the elbows and pointed out the window at {B_nameDef}, who was lying in the grass at noon, watching clouds. "Every day," {A_nameDef} said.\n\n{B_nameDef} says it's called thinking. {A_nameDef} says it's called lying down.

li.label: Side with {A_nameDef}: double shifts for {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is on double shifts until the tally evens out, and {A_nameDef} keeps the count on the wall up to date.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} is on double shifts, and opened the first one by throwing a shovel at {A_nameDef}.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} keep {B_possessive} own pace
li.outcome: People work at different speeds, the council ruled. {B_nameDef} looked pleased with that. {A_nameDef} hasn't spoken to {B_nameDef} since.

li.label: Pair them up on every shift
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now work every shift together. {B_nameDef} is picking up the pace, mostly to make the lecturing stop.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now work every shift together, and {A_nameDef} ends up doing most of {B_nameDef}'s share.

li.label: Stay out of it
li.outcome: The council left them to it, and the complaining has moved from the council room to the dining table.
li.riskOutcome: With the council staying out of it, {A_nameDef} has eased off too, and sees no reason to work harder than the slowest pair of hands.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} swears that {A_nameDef} rode with the raiders who burned {B_possessive} home, years ago and far from here. {A_nameDef} hasn't denied it, and hasn't said anything else either.\n\nThe others are starting to take sides, and the council needs to speak first.

It came out over dinner. {A_nameDef} was telling the story behind an old scar and named the place where {A_pronoun} got it, and {B_nameDef} was on {B_possessive} feet with a knife in hand. {B_nameDef} says {A_nameDef} helped burn that place to the ground.\n\n{A_nameDef} says it was a long time ago, with different people, and that {A_pronoun} was someone else then. The council has to decide whether that's enough.

li.label: The past is past
li.outcome: What {A_nameDef} did before the colony stays before the colony, the council ruled. {B_nameDef} got up from the table and hasn't eaten with the others since.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} heard the ruling, walked out of the meeting, and kept walking.

li.label: {A_nameDef} earns {A_possessive} place
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is working the hardest jobs in the colony, without complaint, until the council is satisfied. {B_nameDef} watches every shift.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} have one swing
li.outcome: The council looked away for one minute. {B_nameDef} used all of it, and {A_nameDef} didn't raise a hand until the very end.

li.label: Keep it between them
li.outcome: It stays between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}, by the council's order. {B_nameDef} agreed to that, and hasn't turned {B_possessive} back on {A_nameDef} since.
li.riskOutcome: By morning the whole story was out. {A_nameDef} has been eating alone since.
